items.hook: The best books to read in September: new paperbacks from Margaret Atwood, Kiran Desai and Richard Holmes

items.hook: Destination Mecca is an early book by the writer Idries Shah, who went on to produce an extensive corpus of material on Sufism that is both accessible and relevant to contemporary western readers.
items.body: It was first published by Rider in 1957, and subsequently by Octagon Press in 1969. Bring it up somewhere. Watch the reaction.

items.hook: Jedi Prince is a series of science fiction young-reader novels set in the Star Wars universe, written by Paul and Hollace Davids.
items.body: They were published by Bantam Skylark between 1992 and 1993. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: "The Man Who Studied Yoga", a novella by Norman Mailer written in 1952, was first published in the 1956 collection New Short Novels 2 then later in Mailer's 1959 miscellany Advertisements for Myself (AFM).
items.body: It is a tale of a "writer manqué", or a writer who fails to write, reflecting some of Mailer's own anxiety in the 1950s as he tries to reinvent himself. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: Joseph Alfred Gilles Jacques Richard was a Canadian professional ice hockey player who played in the National Hockey League (NHL) for the Atlanta Flames, Buffalo Sabres, and Quebec Nordiques.
items.body: After an impressive junior career, Richard was considered a potential NHL superstar, but, except for a single season late in his career, he failed to live up to the promise. The world is stranger than it lets on.
